newsitem.title: CANADA: LUMBER LABOR PACT AGREED IN NORTH BRITISH COLUMBIA.
newsitem.headline: LUMBER LABOR PACT AGREED IN NORTH BRITISH COLUMBIA.

text.p: A tentative labor accord was reached Thursday between the union representing British Columbia lumber workers and the bargaining agent for some companies in the province's northern interior.

IWA-Canada official Harvey Arcand said the three-year contract was substantially the same as the benchmark agreement reached last week between the union and coastal employers. It provides for a five percent wage hike over three years.

The accord reached Thursday covers about 1,800 of the 7,200 unionized lumber workers in the northern interior and was with the Council on Northern Interior Forest Employment Relations (CONIFER), he said.

Arcand said talks would now begin with Weldwood of Canada Ltd and some discussions had already begun with Canfor Corp and Northwood Pulp and Timber Ltd -- companies that do not participate in the northern interior's joint bargaining.
Weldwood is owned by Champion International Corp while Northwood is a joint venture between Noranda Forest Inc and Mead Corp

The union plans to put the contract deals to a ratification vote once agreements are concluded in all areas of the province. Once a coastal accord has been reached, deals elsewhere usually follow soon after.
